title: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek
body:
Read the chapter → [Exodus 17](/bible/exodus/17)

**[Exodus 17:1-4](/bible/exodus/17#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/exodus/17#v1)</sup> And all the congregation of the children of Israel journeyed from the wilderness of Sin, after their journeys, according to the commandment of the Lord, and pitched in Rephidim: and there was no water for the people to drink.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/exodus/17#v2)</sup> Wherefore the people did chide with Moses, and said, Give us water that we may drink. And Moses said unto them, Why chide ye with me? wherefore do ye tempt the Lord?
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/exodus/17#v3)</sup> And the people thirsted there for water; and the people murmured against Moses, and said, Wherefore is this that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst?
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/exodus/17#v4)</sup> And Moses cried unto the Lord, saying, What shall I do unto this people? they be almost ready to stone me.

- At Rephidim there was no water, and the people did chide with Moses: wherefore is this that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst? At the first sign of trial the people jumped off the Lord's bandwagon again, the same as we do today when tribulation comes.
- Moses cried unto the Lord, What shall I do unto this people? they be almost ready to stone me. They were ready to kill the prophet over water, blaming the brother for what only the Most High controls; we have to build our faith up like Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who trusted the Lord even when trials came.

**[Exodus 17:5-7](/bible/exodus/17#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/exodus/17#v5)</sup> And the Lord said unto Moses, Go on before the people, and take with thee of the elders of Israel; and thy rod, wherewith thou smotest the river, take in thine hand, and go.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/exodus/17#v6)</sup> Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink. And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/exodus/17#v7)</sup> And he called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the chiding of the children of Israel, and because they tempted the Lord, saying, Is the Lord among us, or not?

- The Lord stood before Moses upon the rock in Horeb; Moses smote the rock, and water came out of it in the sight of the elders of Israel.
- He called the place Massah and Meribah, temptation and chiding, because they tempted the Lord, saying, Is the Lord among us, or not? That is wickedness: He had just made Egypt dark, slain their firstborn, and sent His angel in the chariot to guide us, and the people still asked whether He was with them. The mercy of the Most High in bearing that is beyond us.

**[Exodus 17:8-13](/bible/exodus/17#v8)**

> <sup>[8](/bible/exodus/17#v8)</sup> Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/exodus/17#v9)</sup> And Moses said unto Joshua, Choose us out men, and go out, fight with Amalek: to morrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the rod of God in mine hand.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/exodus/17#v10)</sup> So Joshua did as Moses had said to him, and fought with Amalek: and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/exodus/17#v11)</sup> And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/exodus/17#v12)</sup> But Moses’ hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/exodus/17#v13)</sup> And Joshua discomfited Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.

- Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim. Amalek was the first nation to come against Israel after Egypt; Amalek was Esau's grandson, born to Eliphaz of Timna the concubine, a duke in the land of Edom.
- When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed. Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands until the going down of the sun. Moses was about eighty years old holding a rod above his head all day; the fathers were mighty men, stronger than we are today.
- The sign shewed the people whose hand their life was in: Moses is the man to hearken to, so do not speak against him. And Joshua discomfited Amalek with the edge of the sword; Joshua was a mighty warrior even then.

  Precepts:
  - **[Genesis 36:12](/bible/genesis/36#v12)**
    > <sup>[12](/bible/genesis/36#v12)</sup> And Timna was concubine to Eliphaz Esau’s son; and she bare to Eliphaz Amalek: these were the sons of Adah Esau’s wife.

    Timna bare to Eliphaz Amalek; Amalek is the grandson of Esau, a duke of Edom.

**[Exodus 17:14-16](/bible/exodus/17#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/exodus/17#v14)</sup> And the Lord said unto Moses, Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/exodus/17#v15)</sup> And Moses built an altar, and called the name of it JEHOVAH–nissi:
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/exodus/17#v16)</sup> For he said, Because the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.

- Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven. Moses wrote it, and [Deuteronomy 25](/bible/deuteronomy/25) is that rehearsal: remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way.
- Amalek smote the hindmost, all that were feeble, when Israel was faint and weary, and he feared not God. He did not meet the mighty men in the front; he went to the back to slay the women, the children, and the old ones. That same spirit works against the nation's young and old today.
- The Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation. By the time Moses rehearsed it in Deuteronomy, forty years had passed and the children of Amalek had done nothing themselves; hundreds of years after that the Lord sent Saul by Samuel to smite Amalek for what was done coming out of Egypt. God be true and every man a liar: the nations do not get away with what they did to His people, and the judgment carries to the seed.
- Saul did not finish Agag's line, and in Esther's day Haman the Agagite of that same seed rose against Israel; the war truly runs from generation to generation.
- Today that seed says they are Jews and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan, robbing Israel of identity and prospering off the oppression. The Lord says He will make them come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee.
- The whole world is set up between Jacob and Esau, and Esau is the end of this world, the so-called white man, with Amalek leading; it is not speaking of the Arab man, for if Ishmael had a rulership still to come, Israel would have another captivity to enter, and Christ has already redeemed us from the curse of the law.
- The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 25:17-19](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v17)</sup> Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt;
    >
    > <sup>[18](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v18)</sup> How he met thee by the way, and smote the hindmost of thee, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary; and he feared not God.
    >
    > <sup>[19](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v19)</sup> Therefore it shall be, when the Lord thy God hath given thee rest from all thine enemies round about, in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance to possess it, that thou shalt blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven; thou shalt not forget it.

    Remember what Amalek did, how he smote the hindmost, the feeble, the faint and weary, and feared not God; thou shalt blot out his remembrance.
  - **[1 Samuel 15:1-3](/bible/1-samuel/15#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/1-samuel/15#v1)</sup> Samuel also said unto Saul, The Lord sent me to anoint thee to be king over his people, over Israel: now therefore hearken thou unto the voice of the words of the Lord.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/1-samuel/15#v2)</sup> Thus saith the Lord of hosts, I remember that which Amalek did to Israel, how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/1-samuel/15#v3)</sup> Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.

    Hundreds of years later the Lord remembered what Amalek did to Israel in the way from Egypt and sent Saul to destroy Amalek utterly.
  - **[Isaiah 14:21-22](/bible/isaiah/14#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/isaiah/14#v21)</sup> Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers; that they do not rise, nor possess the land, nor fill the face of the world with cities.
    >
    > <sup>[22](/bible/isaiah/14#v22)</sup> For I will rise up against them, saith the Lord of hosts, and cut off from Babylon the name, and remnant, and son, and nephew, saith the Lord.

    Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers; the name and remnant are cut off, so none escape by saying it was only the forefathers.
  - **[Revelation 2:9](/bible/revelation/2#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/revelation/2#v9)</sup> I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.

    The blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan; the Most High knows the lie, and Israel in tribulation and poverty is rich.
  - **[Revelation 3:9](/bible/revelation/3#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/revelation/3#v9)</sup> Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee.

    The synagogue of Satan will be made to come and worship before Israel's feet, and to know that the Most High loved Israel.
  - **[2 Esdras 6:7-9](/bible/2-esdras/6#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/2-esdras/6#v7)</sup> Then answered I and said, What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/2-esdras/6#v8)</sup> And he said unto me, From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau.
    >
    > <sup>[9](/bible/2-esdras/6#v9)</sup> For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.

    Jacob's hand held first the heel of Esau; for Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.
  - **[2 Esdras 6:10](/bible/2-esdras/6#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/2-esdras/6#v10)</sup> The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand: other question, Esdras, ask thou not.

    Nothing stands between the heel and the hand; the world passes straight from Esau's end to Jacob's beginning.
  - **[Genesis 3:15](/bible/genesis/3#v15)**
    > <sup>[15](/bible/genesis/3#v15)</sup> And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.

    Enmity is set between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed; the battle between Esau's seed and Israel stands until the end.
  - **[Romans 16:20](/bible/romans/16#v20)**
    > <sup>[20](/bible/romans/16#v20)</sup> And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.

    The God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly; Jacob bruises the head at the end of the world.
